facts.statement: Nasutoceratops lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 76.0 to 75.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous period, about 76.0–75.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first known specimens of Nasutoceratops were discovered in the Kaiparowits Formation of the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument in Utah starting in 2006.
facts.quote: The first known specimens were discovered in Utah in the Kaiparowits Formation of the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument (GSENM) from 2006 onwards

facts.statement: The species Nasutoceratops titusi was formally named in 2013, using a subadult skull as the holotype.
facts.quote: In 2013, the subadult was made the holotype of the new genus and species Nasutoceratops titusi

facts.statement: Eric K. Lund discovered the holotype specimen of Nasutoceratops at locality VP 940 during the 2006 field season.
facts.quote: Among the discoveries that have been made are three new ceratopsian (horned dinosaur) taxa, one of which was identified from UMNH Locality VP 940 discovered by the then graduate student and technician Eric K. Lund during the 2006 field season.

facts.statement: Scott D. Sampson and colleagues described and named Nasutoceratops titusi in 2013.
facts.quote: The paleontologists Scott D. Sampson, Lund, Mark A. Loewen, Andrew A. Farke, and Katherine E. Clayton briefly described and scientifically named the new genus and species Nasutoceratops titusi in 2013

facts.statement: The specific name 'titusi' honors paleontologist Alan L. Titus for his work recovering fossils from the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument.
facts.quote: The specific name titusi is an eponym that honors the paleontologist Alan L. Titus for his important efforts in recovering fossils from the GSENM.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Nasutoceratops is approximately 1.5 meters long.
facts.quote: The holotype skull of Nasutoceratops is approximately 1.5 m long

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops is estimated to have reached a body length of 4.5 meters and a weight of 1.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: its body length has been estimated at 4.5 m, and its weight at 1.5 t.

facts.statement: The brow horns of Nasutoceratops could reach up to 457 mm, making them the longest known among centrosaurines.
facts.quote: they are up to 457 mm, the longest known of any centrosaurine

facts.statement: The neck frill of Nasutoceratops was almost circular, with its widest point located in the middle.
facts.quote: The neck frill is almost circular with its widest point at the middle.

facts.statement: Unlike other centrosaurines, Nasutoceratops had epiossifications shaped like low crescents on the frill margins and one at the midline on top of the frill.
facts.quote: The epiossifications on the margins of the frill are shaped like low crescents, and there is one at the midline at the top of the frill, unlike in other centrosaurines.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the nasal bones of Nasutoceratops were possibly pneumatized (air-filled), a feature unknown in other ceratopsids.
facts.quote: The nasal bones were possibly pneumatized (air-filled), which is unknown in other ceratopsids.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen included an almost complete left forelimb, a fragmentary right forelimb, parts of the pectoral girdle, neck and back vertebrae, and three patches of skin impressions on the left forelimb.
facts.quote: It was collected with an articulated and almost complete left forelimb, an associated yet very fragmentary right forelimb (both lacking hand bones), much of the pectoral girdle, an almost complete syncervical vertebra (the three first neck vertebrae fused together), three associated but fragmentary dorsal vertebrae (of the back), as well as three patches of skin impressions associated with the left forelimb

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops had three horns: one nasal horn above the nasal opening and two brow horns above the eye sockets.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops had three horns; the nasal horn above the nasal opening and the brow horns above the eye sockets.

facts.statement: The external texture of the frill and cheek ossifications was vascularized and rugose, likely covered by a keratinous sheath in life.
facts.quote: Their external texture was very vascularized and rugose, and they were most likely covered by a keratinous sheath when the dinosaur was alive.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Laramidia was divided into separate dinosaur provinces with endemic species, a hypothesis based on the relationship between Nasutoceratops and other contemporaries.
facts.quote: it has been proposed that Laramidia was divided into dinosaur "provinces" with separate endemic species, but this has been contested.

facts.statement: Scott Sampson described the large nose of Nasutoceratops as a "jumbo-sized schnoz" in the museum's press release.
facts.quote: In the UMNH press release accompanying the description of Nasutoceratops, the large nose of the dinosaur was emphasized, with Sampson calling it a "jumbo-sized schnoz".

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops has a bulbous, almost circular snout that expands upwards, resembling the basal centrosaurine Diabloceratops rather than more advanced forms.
facts.quote: The snout region is almost circular overall, which is typical of centrosaurines, but it differs from more derived (or "advanced") centrosaurines and is more similar to the basal (early diverging) Diabloceratops in that it expands upwards, giving the snout region a bulbous appearance.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops likely possesses the shortest snout of any centrosaurine due to abbreviated nasal and maxilla bones.
facts.quote: The shortness of the snout is a result of the abbreviated nasal and maxilla bones, and it may be the shortest of any centrosaurine.

facts.statement: Although the rostral bone is missing, it is inferred to have been triangular in side view, a feature shared with centrosaurines but distinct from chasmosaurines.
facts.quote: The rostral (a bone unique to ceratopsians, which forms the upper beak and contacts the front part of the premaxilla) is not preserved in Nasutoceratops, but by inferring from the contact area of the premaxilla behind it, it has been interpreted as triangular in side view, similar to centrosaurines and unlike chasmosaurines (the other main group of ceratopsids).

facts.statement: Each maxilla of Nasutoceratops is estimated to have held 29 teeth, though it remains unknown whether these teeth were double-rooted or single-rooted.
facts.quote: Each maxilla is estimated to have contained 29 teeth, but it has not been determined whether they were double-rooted as in other ceratopsids or single-rooted as in neoceratopsians.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops possesses a unique double-socketed maxillary flange that slots into the premaxilla to form part of the hard palate.
facts.quote: The maxillary flange at the front of the maxilla, which contributes to the hard palate by slotting into the premaxilla, is double-socketed, a unique feature of Nasutoceratops.

facts.statement: The nasal horn core of Nasutoceratops is low, long, and blade-like, featuring a pinched hind part and a raised, teardrop-shaped expansion at the front.
facts.quote: The nasal horn core that formed the bony part of the horn above the nasal opening is low, long, and blade-like, pinched from side to side along the hind part, and with a somewhat raised, teardrop-shaped expansion at the front.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops likely had hollow, pneumatized nasal bones behind the horn, a feature not previously known in other ceratopsians.
facts.quote: The nasal bones have well-developed internal cavities behind the horn, which suggests they were hollow, and possibly pneumatized (air-filled); pneumatic nasals are unknown in other ceratopsians.

facts.statement: The vaulted skull roof of Nasutoceratops creates the appearance of a forward-facing forehead, a trait shared with Diabloceratops, Albertaceratops, and many chasmosaurines.
facts.quote: The skull roof is very vaulted around the eye region, which gives the impression that Nasutoceratops had a forward facing "forehead" across its width, similar to Diabloceratops and Albertaceratops, as well as many chasmosaurines.

facts.statement: The skull frill of Nasutoceratops was almost circular, reaching its maximum width at the middle section.
facts.quote: The frill is almost circular with its widest point at the middle region.

facts.statement: In the holotype specimen, the skull frill measured approximately 610 mm in length, a size nearly equal to the basal skull.
facts.quote: The total length of the frill of the holotype is around 610 mm, almost equal to the length of the basal skull

facts.statement: The frill featured two large, oval openings known as parietal fenestrae, one located on each parietal bone, a trait common among centrosaurines.
facts.quote: The frill has two large, oval parietal fenestrae, one on each parietal, as is typical for centrosaurines.

facts.statement: Each of the two fenestrae in the frill was approximately 350 mm long, representing about 57% of the total frill length.
facts.quote: The longest axis of each fenestra (from front to back) is about 350 mm long, accounting for about 57% of the frills length

facts.statement: The upper surface of the frill had a saddle shape, curving convexly from side to side and concavely from front to back.
facts.quote: The frill is saddle-shaped, with the upper surface being convex from side to side and concave from front to back

facts.statement: The squamosal bone possessed a high ridge running from the eye socket to the rim, a feature considered unusual for centrosaurines.
facts.quote: The squamosal has a high ridge on its outer surface, running from the direction of the eye socket towards the squamosal rim, which is unusual for centrosaurines

facts.statement: Each parietal bone on the frill margin had seven undulations, with an additional undulation located on the midline at the top.
facts.quote: On each side of the frill, one parietal has seven undulations on the margin, as well as an undulation on the midline at the top of the frill

facts.statement: Unlike most centrosaurines, the frill of Nasutoceratops lacked well-developed hooks and spikes.
facts.quote: The frill lacked the well-developed hooks and spikes that are otherwise typical for centrosaurines.

facts.statement: Although the holotype was not fully grown, researchers consider it unlikely that hooks would have developed later due to the fusion of its epiparietals and other maturity-related bones.
facts.quote: Since the holotype was not fully grown, it is possible such hooks would have developed as it matured, but this is considered unlikely due to the fusion of its epiparietals on the frill and fusion of other bones related to maturity.

facts.statement: The three frontmost neck vertebrae of Nasutoceratops were fused into a single syncervical vertebra, a structure particularly similar to that found in Styracosaurus.
facts.quote: The three frontmost neck vertebrae of ceratopsids were fused into a syncervical vertebra, and that of Nasutoceratops is particularly similar to that of Styracosaurus.

facts.statement: The humerus measured 475 mm in length and featured a prominent deltopectoral crest that accounted for almost half of the bone's total length.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) is 475 mm long, and has a hemispheric humeral head (upper part) and prominent deltopectoral crest, which accounts for of almost half the whole length of the humerus

facts.statement: The ulna was 400 mm long and possessed a large olecranon process serving as the insertion point for the triceps muscle.
facts.quote: The ulna (one of two lower arm bones) is 400 mm long and has a large olecranon process where the triceps muscle inserted.

facts.statement: Three skin impression patches associated with the forelimb covered areas of 120 cm², 84 cm², and 25 cm² respectively.
facts.quote: The patches are identified as patch A, B, and C, and cover 120 cm2, 84 cm2, and 25 cm2, respectively.

facts.statement: The most notable skin impression, Patch C, consisted of raised hexagonal tubercles measuring 8–11 mm in diameter surrounded by triangular grooves.
facts.quote: Patch C, the most notable impression, consists of raised, hexagonal tubercles that measure 8-11 mm in diameter, and are surrounded by triangular grooves.

facts.statement: The unique hexagonal scale pattern on Nasutoceratops resembles 'star' patterns later found on the limbs of Psittacosaurus.
facts.quote: Similar hexagram-like patterns were later observed on the limbs of Psittacosaurus, and have been called "stars".

facts.statement: The frill exhibited a saddle shape with a convex side-to-side curve and a concave front-to-back curve, typical for centrosaurines.
facts.quote: The frill is saddle-shaped, with the upper surface being convex from side to side and concave from front to back, as typical for centrosaurines.

facts.statement: In 2013, researchers assigned Nasutoceratops to the subfamily Centrosaurinae based on specific skull features including a downward-angled premaxilla and a circular nostril region.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops was assigned to Centrosaurinae by Sampson and colleagues in 2013 based on features such as the premaxilla having a pronounced downward angle, the almost circular narial (bony nostril) region, having a spine composed of the nasal and premaxilla, and in having an abbreviated squamosal with a stepped hind margin.

facts.statement: In 2018, the genus Crittendenceratops was described from Arizona and assigned to the clade Nasutoceratopsini.
facts.quote: The paleontologist Sebastian G. Dalman and colleagues named Crittendenceratops in 2018 based on two partial specimens from the Fort Crittenden Formation of Arizona, and assigned the genus to Nasutoceratopsini.

facts.statement: A 2021 analysis suggested that Nasutoceratopsini did not form a natural monophyletic group, instead appearing as an unresolved polytomy of basal centrosaurines.
facts.quote: The 2021 phylogenetic analysis by Dalman and colleagues accompanying the description of the basal centrosaurine Menefeeceratops from the Menefee Formation of New Mexico did not result in Nasutoceratopsini forming a monophyletic (natural) group; all members were found to be basal centrosaurines, forming a polytomy, or unresolved group.

facts.statement: A 2023 analysis by Ishikawa and colleagues recovered Nasutoceratopsini as a natural basal group and placed the genus Furcatoceratops close to Nasutoceratops.
facts.quote: The paleontologist Hiroki Ishikawa and colleagues did recover Nasutoceratopsini as a natural, basal group in their 2023 analysis, and found the new genus Furcatoceratops from the Judith River Formation to be close to Nasutoceratops.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops lived during the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous and coexisted with derived centrosaurines like Styracosaurus and Centrosaurus while retaining primitive features.
facts.quote: But despite dating to the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous, and being contemporary with the derived northern centrosaurines Styracosaurus and Centrosaurus, Nasutoceratops retained more "primitive" features, such as the maxillary tooth row being displaced downward, elongated brow horns, and pronounced epijugals, which were absent in other centrosaurines of the time.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that centrosaurines originated on the island continent of Laramidia 90–80 million years ago, splitting into lineages where Nasutoceratops and Avaceratops evolved enlarged brow horns and reduced frill ornamentation.
facts.quote: Sampson and colleagues stated that the current knowledge indicated that centrosaurines originated on Laramidia (an island continent consisting of what is now western North America) 90–80 million years ago, and that this group split near the base, with most known centrosaurines in one clade from north Laramidia that evolved towards having abbreviated or absent brow horns and more elaborate frills, and Nasutoceratops and Avaceratops in the other, which de-emphasized their frill ornamentation in favor of enlarged brow horns.

facts.statement: The clade containing Nasutoceratops and Avaceratops existed in both northern and southern Laramidia, with Nasutoceratops living approximately 2 million years after Avaceratops.
facts.quote: The late Campanian Nasutoceratops lived about 2 million years later than the early Campanian Avaceratops, and their clade existed in both northern and southern Laramidia.

facts.statement: In 2017, a centrosaurine specimen from Mexico was named Yehuecauhceratops and formally assigned to the clade Nasutoceratopsini.
facts.quote: In 2017, the specimen from Mexico was named Yehuecauhceratops by Rivera-Sylva and colleagues, and formally assigned to Nasutoceratopsini.

facts.statement: In 2013, researchers suggested that Nasutoceratops supported the hypothesis of long-term separation between northern and southern dinosaur communities in Laramidia.
facts.quote: Sampson and colleagues stated in 2013 that the discovery of Nasutoceratops provided support for the "dinosaur provincialism hypothesis", which postulates that there was separation between the fauna of northern and southern Laramidia for more than a million years during the late Campanian

facts.statement: In 2017, researchers argued that the wide distribution of Nasutoceratops across northern and southern Laramidia weakened the theory of distinct provinciality between these regions.
facts.quote: Ryan and colleagues stated in 2017 that the nasutoceratopsin specimen CMN 8804 from Alberta showed that the group persisted in both northern and southern Laramidia, and that their geographically and temporally large distribution weakened the idea that there would have been distinct provinciality between northern and southern Laramidia

facts.statement: The skull shape of Nasutoceratops increased chewing efficiency by positioning the beak closer to the jaw joint.
facts.quote: This morphology increased the mechanical advantage during mastication by moving the beak closer to the joint of the lower jaw

facts.statement: In 2017, researchers proposed that different jaw mechanics allowed Nasutoceratops and other centrosaurines to coexist by reducing competition for food.
facts.quote: Ryan and colleagues proposed in 2017 that differences in jaw mechanics between nasutoceratopsins and centrosaurins may have prevented resource competition, which allowed them to coexist

facts.statement: In 2023, researchers suggested Nasutoceratops may have been solitary or rare in floodplain habitats based on finding only one specimen per quarry.
facts.quote: Ishikawa and colleagues noted in 2023 that only a single nasutoceratopsin specimen was recovered from each quarry in the Judith River Formation, which suggests they were solitary animals or rare in floodplain habitats

facts.statement: In 2017, Nicole Marie Ridgwell described coprolites possibly from Nasutoceratops in the Kaiparowits Formation.
facts.quote: In a 2017 Master's thesis, the paleontologist Nicole Marie Ridgwell described two coprolites (fossilized dung) from the Kaiparowits Formation which, due to their size, may have been produced by a member of one of three herbivorous dinosaur groups known from the formation: ceratopsians (including Nasutoceratops), hadrosaurs, or ankylosaurs

facts.statement: Coprolites attributed to Nasutoceratops contained angiosperm wood, indicating a diet of woody browse.
facts.quote: The coprolites contained fragments of angiosperm wood (which indicates a diet of woody browse)

facts.statement: Coprolites from Nasutoceratops contained traces of mollusc shells, arthropod cuticle, and lizard bones alongside plant material.
facts.quote: The coprolites also contained traces of mollusc shell, arthropod cuticle, and lizard bone that may have been ingested along with the plant material

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops possessed dental batteries with continuously replaced teeth adapted for processing large quantities of fibrous plants.
facts.quote: Ridgwell pointed out that the dental anatomies of ceratopsians and hadrosaurs (with dental batteries comprising continuously replaced teeth) were adapted to process large quantities of fibrous plants

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops is classified as a dinosaur in the order Ornithischia, family Ceratopsidae, and subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote:
regnum: Animalia
phylum: Chordata
classis: Sauropsida
superordo: Dinosauria
ordo: Ornithischia
familia: Ceratopsidae
subfamilia: Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous epoch, specifically the Campanian stage, between 75.9 and 75.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior, durante el Campaniano, entre 75.9 a 75.5 millones de años

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops was a large, four-legged herbivore with a short snout and unique rounded horns above its eyes.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops era un herbívoro cuadrúpedo grande, con un hocico corto y cuernos redondeados únicos sobre sus ojos

facts.statement: The horns of Nasutoceratops extended almost to the tip of its snout and are the longest among all members of the Centrosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Extendiéndose casi hasta la punta de su hocico, estos cuernos son los más largos de todos los miembros de la subfamilia de los Centrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops possessed a unique feature of pneumatic elements in its nasal bones that is unknown in any other ceratopsian.
facts.quote: La presencia de elementos neumáticos en los huesos nasales de Nasutoceratops es un rasgo único y se desconoce en cualquier otra ceratópsido.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops fossils are known from the Kaiparowits Formation in Utah, dating to the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops is known from the Kaiparowits Formation of Utah, which dates to the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous epoch

facts.statement: The sediments of the Kaiparowits Formation where Nasutoceratops was found date to between 75.51 and 75.97 million years ago.
facts.quote: sediments dating to 75.51–75.97 million years ago

facts.statement: The environment of the Kaiparowits Formation was a wet, humid alluvial to coastal plain setting featuring large deep channels, stable banks, and perennial wetlands.
facts.quote: The formation represents an alluvial to coastal plain setting that was wet, humid, and dominated by large, deep channels with stable banks and perennial wetland swamps, ponds, and lakes.

facts.statement: Rare patches of skin were preserved on the forelimb of a Nasutoceratops specimen, a finding uncommon for ceratopsians.
facts.quote: The sandstone that entombed the forelimb preserved patches of skin, which is very rare for ceratopsians

facts.statement: In 2013, Sampson and colleagues noted that the consensus on the function of ceratopsid skull ornamentation was use in intraspecific signaling and combat.
facts.quote: Sampson and colleagues stated in 2013 that while various hypotheses about the function of ceratopsid skull ornamentation have been proposed, the consensus at the time was use in intraspecific signalling and intraspecific combat

facts.statement: Alternative hypotheses for the function of ceratopsid skull ornamentation have included protection against predators and thermoregulation.
facts.quote: Other ideas have ranged from protection against predators and thermoregulation.

facts.statement: Lund and colleagues found that the hypothesis of horn interlocking could not be ruled out for Nasutoceratops based on pathology studies.
facts.quote: Lund and colleagues found that such a hypothesis could not be ruled out for Nasutoceratops.

facts.statement: The body length of Nasutoceratops is estimated at 4.5 meters and its weight at 1.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: La longitud de su cuerpo se ha estimado en 4.5 metros, su peso en 1.5 toneladas.

facts.statement: The snout area around the nasal fossa is strongly developed, representing nearly three-quarters of the skull length compared to the eye sockets.
facts.quote: La parte del hocico alrededor de la fosa nasal está fuertemente desarrollada, representando cerca de tres cuartos de la longitud del cráneo frente a las cuencas de los ojos.

facts.statement: The posterior part of each nasal bone is hollowed out by a large internal cavity.
facts.quote: La parte posterior de cada hueso nasal está ahuecada por una gran cavidad interna.

facts.statement: The brow horns point forward and outward at their bases, then curve inward and finally twist their tips upward.
facts.quote: Los cuernos de las cejas en sus bases apuntan hacia adelante y hacia afuera, luego se curvan hacia adentro y finalmente tuercen sus puntos hacia arriba.

facts.statement: The nasal horn is low and narrow with an elongated base.
facts.quote: El cuerno en la nariz es bajo y estrecho, con una base alargada.

facts.statement: The squamosal has a high crest on its upper surface extending from the eye socket direction to the squamosal edge.
facts.quote: El escamoso tiene una cresta alta en su superficie superior, que va desde la dirección de la cuenca del ojo hacia el borde escamoso.

facts.statement: The frill is roughly circular with its widest point at the mid-edge.
facts.quote: El volante del cráneo es más o menos circular con su punto más ancho en el borde medio.

facts.statement: The osteoderms along the frill edge, epiparietals, and episquamosals are not spike-shaped but resemble simple low crescents.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos en el borde del volante, los epiparietales y los episquamosales, no tienen forma de espigas, sino que tienen la forma de simples medias lunas bajas.

facts.statement: The posterior edge of the frill lacks notches and instead has an epiparietal in the midline.
facts.quote: El borde posterior del volante no tiene muescas, sino que tiene un epiparietal en la línea media.

facts.statement: The snout was short and high, and the nasal bones show internal cavities interpreted as pneumatic excavations invading the bone from the nasal cavity.
facts.quote: El hocico de Nasutoceratops era corto y alto; sus huesos nasales exhiben cavidades internas que los autores consideran que representan excavaciones neumáticas, invadiendo el hueso desde la cavidad nasal.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops had up to 29 tooth positions in the upper jaw, each occupied by several stacked teeth.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops tenía hasta 29 posiciones de dientes en el maxilar, cada una ocupada por varios dientes apilados.

facts.statement: The frontal horns span approximately 40% of the total skull length, nearly reaching the snout tip, and with a bony core length of up to 457 millimeters, they are the largest known in any centrosaurine, both absolutely and relatively.
facts.quote: Las astas de la frente abarcan aproximadamente el 40% de la longitud total del cráneo, casi alcanzando el nivel de la punta del hocico, y con una longitud del núcleo óseo de hasta 457 milímetros son las más grandes conocidas de cualquier centroaurínido, tanto en términos absolutos como relativos.

facts.statement: The jugal bone, or cheekbone, measures 85 millimeters in length, also the largest known among centrosaurines.
facts.quote: El epiyugal, el hueso de las mejillas, tiene una longitud de 85 milímetros, también el más grande conocido entre los centrosaurinídos.

facts.statement: The skull frill is moderately long and perforated by a large kidney-shaped parietal fenestra on each side.
facts.quote: El volante del cráneo es moderadamente largo y perforado por una gran fenestra parietal en forma de riñón a cada lado.

facts.statement: Besides the midline epiparietal, there are seven epiparietals on each side and about four to five episquamosals.
facts.quote: Además de la línea media epiparietal, hay siete epiparietales a cada lado, y alrededor de cuatro a cinco episquamosales.

facts.statement: In the forelimb, the ulna is exceptionally robust with a large olecranon process.
facts.quote: En la extremidad anterior, el cúbito es excepcionalmente robusto con un gran proceso de olécranon.

facts.statement: Its remains were found in Utah, United States.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados en Utah, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: It is known from the holotype UMNH VP 16800, an almost complete skull found in association with a left forelimb, partial anterior dorsal vertebrae, a synsacrum, a pectoral girdle, parts of the right forelimb, and skin impressions, plus referred materials including an adult disarticulated skull (UMNH VP 19466) and an isolated squamosal (UMNH VP 19469).
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir del holotipo UMNH VP 16800, un cráneo casi completo encontrado en asociación y una extremidad izquierda también asociada, tres vértebras dorsales anterior parciales, una sincervical, una cintura escapular, partes de la extremidad anterior derecha e impresiones de la piel y de los materiales referidos UMNH VP 19466, un cráneo adulto desarticulado que consiste en una premaxila, maxilar y nasal incompletas y UMNH VP 19469, un hueso escamoso aislado.

facts.statement: It was discovered and collected in the Kaiparowits Basin Project, started by the University of Utah in 2000, in the middle unit of the Kaiparowits Formation within the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto y recolectado en el Proyecto Cuenca Kaiparowits, iniciado por la Universidad de Utah en 2000, en la unidad media de la Formación Kaiparowits dentro del Monumento Nacional Grand Staircase-Escalante.

facts.statement: It was originally named by Eric Karl Lund, Scott D. Sampson, and Mark A. Loewen in 2011 as "Nasutuceratops", but without official publication, making it a nomen ex dissertatione without validity.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado originalmente por Eric Karl Lund, Scott D. Sampson y Mark A. Loewen en el año de 2011 como "Nasutuceratops", pero aún sin publicarse de manera oficial, por lo que era un nomen ex dissertatione sin validez.

facts.statement: Scott D. Sampson, Lund, Mark A. Loewen, Andrew A. Farke, and Katherine E. Clayton published it officially in 2013, correcting the genus name to Nasutoceratops.
facts.quote: Scott D. Sampson, Lund, Mark A. Loewen, Andrew A. Farke y Katherine E. Clayton realizaron su publicación oficial en 2013, corrigiendo el nombre de género a Nasutoceratops.

facts.statement: The species name honors Alan L. Titus for recovering the Nasutoceratops fossils from the GSENM.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra a Alan L. Titus por recuperar los fósiles de Nasutuceratops del GSENM.

facts.statement: The holotype skull measures approximately 1.5 to 1.8 meters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo del holotipo mide aproximadamente entre 1.5 a 1.8 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops was assigned to the Centrosaurinae in 2013 in a relatively basal position.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops fue asignado a los Centrosaurinae en 2013, en una posición relativamente basal.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Sampson et al. in 2013 discovered that Nasutoceratops was the sister taxon of Avaceratops.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético realizado por Sampson et al. en 2013 descubrió que Nasutoceratops era el taxón hermano de Avaceratops.

facts.statement: Its clade differs from northern centrosaurines in retaining long frontal horns and a short nasal horn, combined with the development, convergent with Chasmosaurinae, of low epiparietals.
facts.quote: Su clado diferiría de los centrosaurinos del norte en la retención de cuernos largos de la frente y un cuerno de nariz corto, combinado con el desarrollo, convergente con los Chasmosaurinae, de epiparietales bajos.

facts.statement: In 2016, this clade was named Nasutoceratopsini, which contains Nasutoceratops, ANSP 15800 (the holotype of Avaceratops), MOR 692 (previously treated as an adult Avaceratops specimen), the newly described CMN 8804 from the Oldman Formation, and another undescribed ceratopsian found in Malta, Montana.
facts.quote: En 2016, este clado se llamó Nasutoceratopsini, el cual contiene a Nasutoceratops, así como ANSP 15800, el holotipo de Avaceratops, MOR 692, previamente tratado como un espécimen adulto de Avaceratops, el recién descrito CMN 8804 de la Formación Oldman y otro ceratopsio no descrito encontrado en Malta, Montana.

facts.statement: Argon-argon dating indicates the Kaiparowits Formation was deposited between 76.1 and 74.0 million years ago, during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: La datación radiométrica de argón-argón indica que la Formación Kaiparowits fue depositada entre 76.1 y 74.0 millones de años atrás, durante la etapa del Campaniense del Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, the Kaiparowits Formation site was located near the western coast of the Niobrara Sea, a large inland sea that divided North America into two landmasses: Laramidia to the west and Appalachia to the east.
facts.quote: Durante el período Cretácico Superior, el sitio de la Formación Kaiparowits estaba ubicado cerca de la costa occidental del mar de Niobrara, un gran mar interior que dividió a América del Norte en dos masas de tierra, Laramidia al oeste y Appalachia hacia el este.

facts.statement: The plateau where the dinosaurs lived was an ancient floodplain dominated by large channels and abundant wetlands, peat bogs, ponds, and lakes, and was surrounded by highlands.
facts.quote: La meseta donde vivían los dinosaurios era una antigua llanura de inundación dominada por grandes canales y abundantes humedales, pantanos de turba, estanques y lagos, y estaba rodeada de tierras altas.

facts.statement: The climate was humid and warm and supported a wide and diverse range of organisms.
facts.quote: El clima era húmedo y cálido y soportaba una amplia y diversa gama de organismos.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops shared its paleoenvironment with theropods such as dromaeosaurids, the troodontid Talos sampsoni, ornithomimids like Ornithomimus velox, tyrannosaurids like Albertosaurus and Teratophoneus, armored ankylosaurids, the duck-billed dinosaurs Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus and Gryposaurus monumentensis, the ceratopsids Utahceratops gettyi and Kosmoceratops richardsoni, and the oviraptorosaurian Hagryphus giganteus.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops compartió su paleoambiente con terópodos como dromeosáuridos, el troodóntido Talos sampsoni, ornitomímidos como Ornithomimus velox, tiranosáuridos como Albertosaurus y Teratophoneus, anquilosáuridos blindados, los dinosaurios pico de pato Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus y Gryposaurus monumentensis, los ceratópsidos Utahceratops gettyi y Kosmoceratops richardsoni y el ovirraptorosaurio Hagryphus giganteus.

facts.statement: This is notable because pneumatic nasals are unknown in any other ceratopsian, supporting that this feature represents a unique derived trait of this genus.
facts.quote: Esto es notable porque los nasales neumáticos son desconocidos en cualquier otro ceratopsido, lo que respalda que esta característica representa un rasgo derivado único de este género.

facts.statement: The curved disposition of the horizontally projected brow horn was compared to that of modern cattle by paleontologist David Hone.
facts.quote: La disposición curva del cuerno de la ceja proyectada horizontalmente fue comparada con la del ganado moderno por el paleontólogo David Hone.

facts.statement: According to this study, the existence of Nasutoceratops would support the hypothesis of fauna separation between the north and south of Laramidia.
facts.quote: Según este estudio, la existencia de Nasutoceratops apoyaría la hipótesis de la separación de fauna entre el norte y el sur de Laramidia.
